title: Icp
comment: Icp — Iterative closest point is one of the basic algorithms for rigid shape registration. Leverages the closed form formula of least square rigid motion. Can be coupled with optimal transport (e.g. Hungarian algorithm). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_closest_point

title: Pinsker
comment: Pinsker — Pinsker's inequality is a fundamental inequality of information theory. Bounds the total variation norm by the relative entropy (also known as KL divergence). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinsker%27s_inequality

title: Sdp Optim
comment: Sdp Optim — One can encode or approximate convex shapes as intersections of the semi-definite positive cone and affine spaces (linear matrix inequalities). This allows one to use interior point methods to solve optimization on these sets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_matrix_inequality

title: Qr
comment: Qr — The QR decomposition can be computed in a numerically stable way using planar rotation matrices. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Givens_rotation

title: Svd
comment: Svd — The SVD decomposes the action of a matrix into rotations and scalings along the axes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singular_value_decomposition
alt_text: Svd. The SVD decomposes the action of a matrix into rotations and scalings along the axes.

title: Monotone
comment: Monotone — Monotone operators (Minty, Browder) generalize monotone functions. (sub)-gradients of convex functions are (maximal) monotone. Skew-symmetric (gradients of min-max) operators are also monotone. These are the two extremal cases (Asplund). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monotonic_function

title: Weierstrass
comment: Weierstrass — The Weierstrass function is continuous if a<1 but nowhere differentiable if ab 1. The Hausdorff dimension of its graph was conjectured by Mandelbrot in 1977 and proved by Shen in 2016. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weierstrass_function

title: Reaction Diffusion
comment: Reaction Diffusion — Reaction-diffusions are nonlinear PDEs which describe the formation of a surprisingly rich family of patterns. Introduced by Alan Turing in 1952. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reaction%E2%80%93diffusion_system

title: Rkhs 001
comment: Rkhs 001 — Reproducing Kernel Hilbert spaces define norms on functions so that solutions of regularized fitting problems are linear sum of kernel functions. Defines non-parametric learning methods (complexity scales with input). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproducing_kernel_Hilbert_space

title: Ot Gaussians
comment: Ot Gaussians — The Optimal Transport geometry of 1-D Gaussians is flat in the (mean, std) plane. In particular, the OT interpolation is a linear interpolation of mean and std.

title: W1 Graphs 001

title: Banach Fixed Point
comment: Banach Fixed Point — Banach fixed point theorem ensures existence of a unique fixed point for contracting maps. The proof is constructive by iterating the map. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banach_fixed-point_theorem
